page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory footprint comprises 64 GB of RAM, conforming to a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB allocated per virtual core. The instance includes no integrated local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on external network block storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent mid-tier multi-threaded execution, alongside constrained single-core and uncached memory metrics. Multi-threaded throughput is demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 31,611.76, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,281.0, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 12,260.17. In contrast, single-threaded operations show lower relative capability, with stress-ng single-core testing scoring 766.88 and Geekbench single-core reaching 1,306.0. Memory transfers reach 1,571.99 GB/sec for small cached blocks, but fall to 35.37 GB/sec read and 16.73 GB/sec write on uncached 256 MB blocks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency standpoint, the ecs.c6a.8xlarge balances dense multi-core processing against a lean memory allocation, avoiding the expense of oversized RAM allocations or local NVMe storage. Testing confirms practical capability for parallelized application workloads, achieving 27.12 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 7.74 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. It is functionally aligned with workloads such as software compilation pipelines, distributed web services, containerized backend applications, and parallelized data transformation jobs.

It supplies 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores paired with 64 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration features an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without integrated local storage or GPU acceleration. In benchmark assessments, the instance demonstrates dependable multi-threaded performance, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 31,611.76, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,281.0, and static web serving throughput of 7.74 GB/sec, offset by lower single-threaded metrics and uncached memory bandwidth. This hardware setup offers practical compute density for parallel workloads that do not demand extensive RAM per core, making it well matched for Clang software compilation, multi-threaded batch operations, intermediate data processing, and scalable web tier serving.
